compute.reported_as: For the neural network, we use psi_KL in all simulations and consider three different values for the number hidden variables M consisting of 2, 2.5 and 3 times of the number of spins N = L^2 in the system. [...] we implement the conjugate gradient method to solve the system of equations, Eq.(12). To stabilize the method, we introduce a ridge parameter lambda = 1e-6. For each training step, we collect 10000 samples to evaluate averages as mentioned in Sec. 3.2 including the variational energy and log derivatives. [...] The typical value for N_skip is from 30 to 100. As for evaluation, we collect 2 x 10^5 samples to calculate the average and statistical error. The learning rate used in the training ranges from 5e-4 to 3e-2. [...] For large L, to save training time, we initialize the parameters W in psi_KL using the parameters trained by means of the cheaper wave function psi_s. All simulations are performed using Eigen and Intel MKL on Intel E5-2680v4 and AMD Rome 7702 CPU nodes.
compute.source: Sec. 3.4 'Implementation details'; Sec. 3.3 ('a good approximation of the ground state can be achieved after hundreds or thousands iterations'); Sec. 5 Limitations ('The computational cost of a single training step scales as O(N_sample x M N^2)'), arXiv:2206.14307 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: One blanket statement for all simulations in the paper. samples = 10000 Monte Carlo samples per training step; a separate 2e5 samples are used for the final evaluation. Parameter count not stated as a number: RBM with M = 2N, 2.5N or 3N complex hidden units (weights W only, biases removed for spin-flip symmetry), symmetrized over translations and C4v (psi_KL); which M produced each table entry is not stated. Iteration count only as 'hundreds or thousands iterations'. No wall-clock, core count, node count or GPU use stated.
